human_review_reasons: The ablation latency in claim-014 is labeled as real-hardware evidence, but the source does not identify the physical device for Table 6; the matching 47 ms value suggests Jetson Orin Nano but does not establish the execution environment explicitly.

objective_assessments.reason: The supported record covers multiple central EDGE topics: a distilled and quantized diffusion architecture, direct latency and memory measurements on two edge platforms, and application-specific on-device visual anonymization.

Supported evidence spans three datasets, several task-specific baseline tables, two physical edge platforms, downstream-utility measurements, and controlled component ablations; the supplied record does not establish unusually complete reproducibility or coverage beyond 640 by 480.

The supported tables show consistent latency and throughput advantages against multiple named baselines on two devices, while privacy, perceptual-quality, downstream-utility, resolution, and memory tradeoffs remain visible.

The source reports direct on-device latency and peak-memory measurements over 1,000 frames on both an embedded GPU platform and a mobile SoC at a stated resolution; energy, thermal behavior, and higher-resolution operation are not measured.

assumptions: The suggested patch-level parallel or cascaded variants can be implemented on the reported devices.
The reported privacy, perceptual-quality, latency, and memory metrics can be reused to compare higher-resolution variants.
A suitable adversarial reconstruction protocol can be specified even though the source does not provide one.
objective_assessments.reason: A concrete next experiment is to test the paper's suggested higher-resolution architectural adaptations on the same two edge platforms while retaining the reported privacy, quality, latency, and memory comparisons; adversarial reconstruction testing supplies a second bounded direction.

verdicts.reason: The quoted abstract states that surveillance anonymization requires effectiveness and computational efficiency, especially on resource-constrained edge devices.
The Figure 2 caption explicitly identifies PII detection, latency-optimized diffusion anonymization, and category-aware fidelity control as the three framework stages.
The source explicitly describes progressive distillation from approximately 1,000 diffusion steps to 4-8 steps.
The source states that redundant channels are pruned, 8-bit quantization is applied, and the resulting memory-footprint reduction is 2.4 times.

The source makes the controller depend jointly on user privacy preference and device latency slack, and explicitly attaches current device load to mask expansion and backbone compression; the claim attributes all four controls only to device load.
The abstract names COCO-Privacy, Cityscapes-Privacy, and VIRAT-Privacy as experimental datasets.
The experimental setup states that average wall-clock latency and peak memory were measured directly on-device over 1,000 frames at 640 by 480 resolution.
Table 2 reports the stated Privacy Accuracy, SSIM, LPIPS, and detection mAP values, each better in the indicated direction than every listed baseline.
Table 3 reports the stated PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS, and detection-mAP-drop values, each better in the indicated direction than the listed scene-text baselines.
Table 4 reports 45.0 percent readability, 0.10 LPIPS, and a 3.0-point detection-mAP drop for EdgeDiffusion, all improved over the two listed baselines.

Table 5 reports exactly the stated latency, throughput, and peak-memory values at 640 by 480 on Jetson Orin Nano and Snapdragon 8 Gen 2, and the setup identifies these as direct on-device measurements.
Table 1 reports the stated 1.2-point COCO mAP drop and 2.0-point Cityscapes mIoU drop, both smaller than those of the listed anonymization baselines.
Table 6 reports the stated Privacy Accuracy decrease from 97.0 to 93.0 percent and LPIPS increase from 0.098 to 0.11 when adaptive fidelity control is removed.

Table 6 supports the 47-to-260 ms latency change and 97.0-to-96.0 percent Privacy Accuracy change, but neither the table nor its surrounding ablation text identifies the physical device used for that latency measurement, so `real_hardware` is not tied to an exact execution environment.
The limitations section states that all experiments use 640 by 480 resolution and that higher resolutions may require architectural adaptations to retain real-time edge throughput.
The limitations section explicitly says robustness against attacks that reverse anonymization to recover identities has not been evaluated.
